subject: phoenix
reasoning:
I'm planning out a single TypeScript module using the SDK to build a stylized phoenix model in a resting pose, thinking through proportions like wingspan and body size to keep it realistic yet mythical.

I'm sketching the coordinate layout: legs with thigh, shin, and tarsus segments planted at y=0, a body centered around y~0.55, neck rising to a head near y~0.95, a long trailing tail of feather cards, and wings extending outward with feathered edges—then starting to define the builder configuration for the model.

Defining the joint hierarchy now: a root hip joint, a spine chain curving upward and forward through a few points toward the chest, and beginning the neck chain to connect up to the head.

Adding more joint definitions...

Now I'm thinking about eyes as small spheres attached to the head bone, and the body as a sweep along the spine chain with varying radii at each joint to give it a tapered shape.

For coloring, I'm considering a gradient paint going from gold at the belly to red-orange toward the back, maybe with a flame-like custom paint function based on vertical position. Then I'll move on to defining the wing joints attached to the chest.

Setting up shoulder joints and wing chain geometry...

Writing feather SVG markup...

Now I'm figuring out how to map cards onto the wing chain, sampling points along the chain at several t-values to get frames, then feeding those into the cards function with size, lean, and flow parameters to orient each feather. I'm working through how the lean angle relates to each frame's facing axis along the chain's tangent direction.

This orientation is getting tangled—the card ends up perpendicular to the wing surface instead of lying flat against it. I'm reconsidering the approach entirely, maybe simplifying to a more direct method for placing feather fans along the wing's trailing edge.

I'll place feathers by looping over wing positions, using wing.at(t) to get chain points as anchors for each extruded feather, with weights derived from the chain point for rigid attachment. Keeping the overall code to roughly 200 lines, I'm now working out the leaf-shaped outline for each feather.

Writing feather outline points...

Adding tail feather chain...

Computing plume orientations...

Plotting leg chains with hip, knee, ankle, and toe joints for digitigrade-style legs, bending back for a bird-like stance.

So I'll name the joints hipL, kneeL, ankleL, toeL for the leg chain, with the tip resting at the ground contact point for the toe. Now I'm defining a tapering radius profile for the leg sweep, shrinking from thigh to ankle.

Adding small capsule-based toes and talons at the foot, branching a few rods from the ankle point toward the ground for a clawed look.

Now I'm moving to the head: placing a sphere-ish shape at the head joint, then adding flame-like crest spikes sweeping back from the skull for a fiery phoenix silhouette.

For the body sweep radius, I'll vary thickness along the spine with a sine curve so it's thicker in the middle. For coloring, I'll use a countershade paint that blends a darker red on the back with a golden belly tone, applying it to both the body and neck for consistency.

Now I'm mapping out the wing skeleton — placing a shoulder joint and defining a chain of wing points curving outward and back, naming segments like wingL1 through wingTipL, and working out how the spine joints (waist, chest) connect as parents for these chains.

Continuing the neck segment with two joints, neck1 at the base and neck2 partway up, so the head should attach to neck2 near the top before connecting onward.

Now I'm working out the wing chain, deciding to parent the first wing joint directly to the chest rather than adding a separate shoulder joint, since the chain-building logic already handles that attachment. I'm laying out the wing path points from shoulder through elbow and wrist, naming the joints shoulderL, elbowL, and wristL for the left wing.

For symmetry, I plan a makeWing helper that mirrors the x-coordinate with a sign flag so the right wing matches the left. Then I'm figuring out how to attach feather shapes along the wing chain at several points, deciding their width and droop direction so the primaries hang naturally below the wing edge.

Now I'm giving the feathers a flame-colored gradient to tie into the phoenix theme, while keeping the body countershaded, and sketching out how to sweep the wing itself as a thin tapered rod with its own color.

Designing the feather shape as an outline generator function that produces a pointed plume tapering from base to tip, which I'll extrude along the wing curve using color, thickness, and position parameters.

Setting up the tail chain with four points tapering down from the waist, naming them tailA through tailEnd, then planning plume feathers spaced along the tail at increasing t values.

For the plumes' orientation, I'm working out the extrusion plane -- deciding to keep the x-axis fixed sideways while varying the y-axis angle vertically so the feathers fan out at different pitch angles rather than laterally.

Computing the plume positions...

Now I'm working out the head details - crest spikes, and positioning the beak as a cone from the jaw joint near the head sphere's front edge.

Defining jaw joint parameters...

Now I'm positioning the upper and lower beak spikes with slightly offset coordinates and radii, then placing the eye spheres relative to the head sphere's center.

Shaping the body sweep along the spine chain with a radius function that tapers from hips to chest, aiming for an egg-shaped torso profile.

Now I'm planning the neck, head, and leg sweeps—using a sphere-based head with a crest, and thinning leg radii from top to bottom. I need to double-check the joint hierarchy, since the hips and waist both sit at the same root position, so I should clarify which one anchors the leg chain.

I'm now working through the skeleton structure to avoid a zero-length bone at the hip-waist junction—deciding whether to introduce a separate pelvis root joint slightly offset from the spine's first joint, so the spine and leg chains both parent cleanly without overlapping at the same point.

Setting leg joint coordinates for hip, knee, ankle, and toe with slight bends for a natural stance, making sure the toe touches the ground at y=0 while keeping leg width inside the pelvis radius.

Writing symmetric limb helper...

I'm weighing whether to add extra wow-factor details like embers or feather textures, but deciding to keep things simple and skip SVG feather cards on the wings to avoid rendering risk, settling on reasonable overall proportions for the phoenix.

Now I'm assembling the final code, importing the builder and paint utilities, using rng for subtle jitter in the tail plumes' length, and setting up the countershaded body paint and flame gradient colors.

Then I'm building out the skeleton structure, creating the pelvis joint and a spine chain with named segments connecting waist, back, and chest, along with head geometry and beak coloring.

Adjusting the neck path coordinates...

The spine joints (waist, back, chest) each span their own segment, with chest running into the neck. I'm placing the head joint at the neck tip with a slight forward tilt, then adding a jaw joint parented to the head.

For wings, I'm building a symmetric left/right chain function: each wing runs from shoulder through elbow and wrist to a fingertip, parented at the chest, then swept with a radius to give it thickness.

Then I'm adding feathers along each wing by sampling several points along its length and extruding plume shapes oriented outward, tweaking the axis vectors so they orient correctly relative to the wing's surface.

I'll make feather length grow toward the tip, with primaries longest, and have feathers hang from points along the wing spine. Now I'm starting to define the tail chain with its spine coordinates.

Working out the fan angle for the plumes so they spread outward along the tail, placing them at increasing positions toward the tail's end so they trail backward naturally.

I'm reconsidering the plume geometry—each blade sits in a plane with lateral width and a back/down length, so the sheet's normal points roughly upward, making it a vertical-ish fan of blades rather than flat horizontal feathers. I need to double check the width direction is actually perpendicular to the plume's length axis for the fan to read correctly from the side.

Good enough, moving on to legs now — I'm building a chain for each leg with hip, knee, and foot joints parented to the pelvis.

Still building leg and toe geometry... now moving to the head, adding a sphere shape positioned and parented appropriately.

For the eyes, I'm placing small dark spheres symmetrically on either side of the head, and considering adding a gold iris ring with a highlight for extra detail.

Now I'm working on crest spikes jutting from the back of the head, defining their base positions and directions to flare outward like flame shapes.

For the beak, I'm placing a tapered spike from a base point near the face to a tip point further out, checking the spike function's parameter order for tip versus direction-and-length.

Now I'm thinking about adding small ember particle spheres scattered near the wing tips and tail ends for extra detail, using tiny icosahedron geometries in gold/flame tones.

Then I'll finalize the function to return the built rig root, making sure the Three.js import and export structure are correct.

I'm double-checking the helper signatures—part, sweep, extrude, and the plume curve types—to confirm they all accept the point and color arguments I'm passing in correctly.

Now I'm verifying that all joint and chain names across the wings, legs, spine, and neck are valid and unique, since duplicates or bad characters would break the skeleton structure.

I'm checking each chain's point count against its name count to make sure spans and segment names line up correctly for spine, neck, tail, wing, and leg chains, confirming the chest-to-wing parenting order comes after the spine is built.

Now I'm verifying the neck-to-head joint handoff positions and sizes, checking the flame gradient's clamp boundary on the feathers, confirming the countershade coloring between back and belly, and reviewing the pelvis direction input before looking at a potential joint issue.

I'm defining a helper function to generate plume point arrays for the feather shapes, confirming the winding order and bevel settings work together, then seeding a random generator for tail length variation and setting up ember geometry before finalizing the full export with metadata.
